observation.visible_scene: A wide landscape shot: a large snow-streaked mountain peak dominates the upper-left/center background, with a band of low cloud/mist hugging its right flank and scattered white clouds in the blue sky at the top right. A row of dark green conifer trees lines the far shore of a calm, mirror-like lake that fills the lower third of the frame; the trees and mountain are reflected in the still water. A soft pinkish-purple sun glow and a circular lens flare sit on the left edge. A faint 'proArtInc' watermark is visible at the bottom left.
visible_changes: Across all sampled frames (t=0.000 to t=3.333 s) the mountain, the central tall tree, the right-hand tree cluster, the sky clouds, the mist on the slope, the left-side lens flare, and the water reflections hold the same positions and shapes; no translation, expansion, or deformation of these elements is detectable between the first and last frames.

The overall composition is effectively static; the camera viewpoint does not shift (background and foreground landmarks do not move relative to the frame edges), so no pan, tilt, or zoom is supported.
Any water-surface ripple or slow cloud drift, if present, is not resolvable at this frame spacing; the reflections look unchanged frame to frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the source video contains wind-driven tree sway, moving clouds, or camera motion beyond this cropped window.
The cause of the lens flare / sun position (time of day) is not shown.
What happens before t=0 or after t=3.333 s is unknown.
uncertain_details: Possible very subtle shimmering of the lake reflection or faint cloud movement cannot be confirmed from these samples.
Camera motion is treated as absent/uncertain because the background gives no evidence of translation or scale change.
The scene is a still or near-still landscape rather than an action sequence; no onset, contact, or completion is observable.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
